questions.q: According to this lesson, what mechanism underlies Snowflake's cross-platform agent interoperability story?
options: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the same managed MCP server used for any single integration, reused as the connection point for every platform
A separate, Snowflake-proprietary Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol
Direct database replication between vendor platforms
Manual CSV export/import between each platform
questions.explain: Snowflake's own materials are consistent that interoperability runs through MCP rather than a separate agent-to-agent protocol layered on top.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, named platform this lesson describes as connecting to Snowflake via MCP?
options: Salesforce Agentforce, with native MCP client support reaching beta in January 2026
A fictional product with no real-world deployment
A protocol that competes with MCP rather than using it
A tool unrelated to AI agents entirely
questions.explain: Agentforce's native MCP client support launched in pilot in mid-2025 and reached beta by January 2026, letting it connect to any MCP-compliant server including Snowflake.

questions.q: What four-step shape does this lesson describe for connecting an external platform to Snowflake's Cortex tools?
options: Build the Cortex service, expose it via the MCP server, add an MCP connector on the external platform, authenticate via OAuth
Export all data to CSV, email it, re-import it, then delete the original
Disable RBAC, connect directly to the database, re-enable RBAC
Build a custom SDK unique to each external platform
questions.explain: The same four steps repeat regardless of which external platform is connecting, because every platform already speaks MCP as a client.

questions.q: Why didn't platforms like Copilot Studio, Agentforce, and UiPath need a Snowflake-specific SDK to connect?
options: Because they already speak MCP as clients, and Snowflake exposes its tools through a standard MCP server
Because Snowflake built a custom bridge for each one individually
Because none of them actually support connecting to Snowflake
Because MCP is a Snowflake-only protocol that other vendors licensed
questions.explain: MCP is an open standard; any MCP-aware client can discover and call tools from any MCP-aware server without a bespoke integration per pair.

questions.q: What is the honest, accurate way to describe Snowflake's agent interoperability approach, per this lesson?
options: MCP, not a separate agent-to-agent (A2A) protocol
A2A protocol exclusively, with no MCP involved
Both MCP and A2A are used interchangeably with no distinction
Neither MCP nor A2A — it is entirely proprietary
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly cautions against claiming Snowflake supports a separate A2A protocol — the real mechanism is MCP.
